RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent slot9 is basically TFT with some extra: starts C, if opponent D then D, with some forgiveness? Actually parent code: ... So it's TFT, punishes D, but if opponent has 3 D in last6, it defects even if last C. It has no forgiveness after D. Hence stuck against one_D_TFT. Measure says not_recovered=1.0. So we need forgiveness after single D. Parent also doesn't exploit ALLC. So improvement: forgive single D to recover, and exploit ALLC."
STRATEGY: The parent is a TFT-like strategy that punishes defection and gets stuck against one_D_TFT/four_D_TFT, while recovering against four_D_ALLC. The trace simulates the parent and proposed variants against controlled probes (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) and classic IPD strategies. It changes the strategy by adding forgiveness after a single defection, probing/exploiting always-cooperators, defecting on the last round, and breaking long DD streaks.

The trace simulates it against four_D_TFT, ALLD, four_D_ALLC, one_D_TFT, and periodic_D. It changes the forgiveness logic to a two-round forgiveness after a 4+ opponent defection streak, adds ALLC exploitation, and adds last-round defection.

STRATEGY: The parent defects when the last six opponent actions contain at least three defections, forgives single defections, and exploits unconditional cooperators. The trace simulates the parent against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D, and TFT, then revises the exploitation rule so it only keeps defecting after an opponent cooperates if that opponent has already cooperated after at least two prior defections.
